articles.title: IF YOU MISSED JOHN DOBSON
articles.summary: This article reports on a visit by John Dobson, the pioneer of cheap, everyman telescopes, to the Club on May 9. During his talk, Dobson covered telescope making, public observing, cosmology, and philosophy, engaging the audience with fun, controversy, and stories. He offered insights into his telescope designs, including a notable critique of white telescope tubes for their thermal inconsistencies.

articles.title: JUNE
articles.summary: The document outlines a schedule of astronomy-related events for June, primarily hosted by the SJAA. Activities include multiple star parties at Houge Park and Fremont Peak, a general meeting featuring a discussion on CCD imaging, an astronomy class focusing on deep-sky observing, and a weekend trip to Yosemite National Park.

articles.title: JULY
articles.summary: This document outlines the schedule of events for July, primarily featuring multiple star parties at Houge Park and Fremont Peak, along with a general meeting and an astrophotography class. Key details like sunset times and moon phases are provided for observing events. The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) also includes a note on insurance coverage for its sponsored events.

articles.title: TRUE FACTS ABOUT FREMONT PEAK
articles.summary: This article clarifies new access policies at Fremont Peak, as communicated by Ranger Mike. The gate to the observatory area will be locked, with the combination available exclusively to FPOA members, allowing them to drive and park there. Non-FPOA members can still access the area on foot, and the $3 per vehicle astronomy fee remains for everyone, with flexible overnight stay rules.

articles.title: Dobson, from p. 1
articles.summary: This article details a presentation by John Dobson, highlighting his deep engagement in public astronomy, his unique perspectives on cosmology, and his philosophical views. Dobson critiqued the Big Bang theory, advocating for a Steady State model, and illustrated complex scientific concepts with elegant analogies. The author emphasizes Dobson's dedication, engaging presentation style, and his significant, albeit sometimes controversial, influence on amateur astronomy.

articles.title: THE SHALLOW SKY
articles.summary: This article provides a monthly guide to planetary visibility for June, detailing which planets are observable. Mercury and Mars are too close to the Sun, while Venus is a morning object. Jupiter returns to late-night viewing and features an occultation by the Moon on June 17. Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune are visible in the morning or throughout the night, with Pluto presented as a challenging target for observers.

articles.title: Fremont Peak, from p. 1
articles.summary: The article clarifies fee policies for Fremont Peak State Park, stating a $3 fee for nighttime astronomical use and a $7 camping fee, with formal written approval pending. Park management is addressing issues with unruly visitors by encouraging reporting incidents and discussing potential measures like a locked gate at Doc Flat for astronomers. The astronomy community is invited to provide input on ensuring fee payment and minimizing disturbances.

articles.title: LUNACY
articles.summary: This article, titled "LUNACY" by David North, provides a guide to lunar observing opportunities for June, following a previous introductory event. It details specific dates and phenomena, including the first quarter on June 1st, full Moon on the 9th, and new Moon around the 23rd/24th, along with specific librations of the western and southern limbs. The author also highlights unique viewing experiences like Sinus Iridum appearing on the "dark side" and offers tips for observing features like the Orientale area and southern craters.

articles.title: THE CELESTIAL TOURIST SPEAKS - ON APOLLO
articles.summary: This article recounts the human involvement in the Apollo program, detailing that twelve individuals walked on the Moon across six missions (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17). It clarifies that while twenty-seven 'seats' were available for lunar voyages, only twenty-four unique individuals made the trip, with three astronauts traveling twice. The piece also mentions other Apollo missions, including test flights, Skylab missions, and the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project, distinguishing them from lunar landing attempts.

articles.title: EDITOR'S EXTRAS
articles.summary: The article recounts the hectic coordination of John Dobson's talk, detailing the logistical challenges of his travel, a critical mirror aluminizing appointment, and meeting schedules. It offers a humorous and personal account of Dobson's quirky personality, highlighting his specific dietary habits, clever conversational tactics, and resourceful nature, providing a memorable behind-the-scenes look at the astronomy icon.

articles.title: ACTIVITIES THROUGH OTHER CLUBS
articles.summary: This article outlines various astronomy activities and observing opportunities offered by different clubs. TAC provides access to the Montebello site on Wednesdays and organizes mobile first-quarter star parties, as well as third-quarter parties at Van Meter school, with event details available on their webpage. PAS hosts public viewing every clear Friday evening at Foothill Observatory with a 16-inch reflector and 6-inch refractor, and solar viewing on clear Saturday mornings, encouraging all SJAA members to participate.

articles.title: June
articles.summary: The June schedule for PAS includes a General Meeting on June 12 featuring a presentation on the Apollo 13 accident by Owen Brown. A Board Meeting is set for June 17, and a private observing night for members will take place on June 20 at the Oakridge site.

articles.title: July
articles.summary: This document lists two upcoming events for July: a PAS General Meeting themed "Instruments Night" on July 10th and a PAS Board Meeting on July 15th. Both events are scheduled to take place at Foothill College, with the board meeting specifically at the observatory. The content originates from a June 1998 publication, likely an ephemeris.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article reports on new comet discoveries, including two found by the SOHO satellite and one by amateur astronomer Patrick Stonehouse, who made his first discovery after 100 hours of casual comet hunting over 20 years. It provides detailed ephemerides and orbital elements for four comets: C/1997 J2 (Meunier-Dupouy), C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), C/1998 H1 (Stonehouse), and C/1998 J1 (SOHO), offering observational data for astronomers.

articles.title: Richard Stanton
articles.summary: This document, an astronomical ephemeris for June 1998 compiled by Richard Stanton and Don Machholz (with times in PDT), provides detailed celestial mechanics data. It outlines lunar phases, planetary positions including rise, transit, and set times, right ascension, and declination for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The guide also includes information on the Sun, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights observing conditions for a 'Darkest Saturday Night'.

articles.title: May Board Meeting Notes
articles.summary: The May 1998 SJAA board meeting covered potential observatory developments at Pacheco State Park and Fremont Peak, along with updates to the club's C11 telescope and loaner program. Key decisions included approving Astronomical League dues, changing the swap meet start time, and publishing preliminary minutes. The board also addressed a negative public outreach experience, emphasizing the importance of making attendees feel welcome, and began discussing rebuilding the observatory fund.

articles.title: To Subscribe to/Unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List send mail to
articles.summary: This document provides simple instructions for managing a subscription to the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) mailing list. Users can subscribe or unsubscribe by sending an email with a blank subject line and either "subscribe" or "unsubscribe" in the body to sjaa-request@seds.org.

articles.title: PERIODICAL PUBLICATION STATEMENT
articles.summary: This document serves as the official periodical publication statement for "SJAA Ephemeris," the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It confirms that the newsletter is published 12 times annually, spanning from January through December, and provides the association's mailing address.

articles.title: SUBMIT
articles.summary: This document encourages members to submit articles for publication in the *SJAA Ephemeris* newsletter. Submissions should be sent via email to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com by the tenth of the month to be included in the following month's issue. Contributors are asked to include their name and phone number with their articles.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors for an organization. It provides the names, titles (President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, and Directors), and phone numbers for each leadership position.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document lists the staff members responsible for an 'Ephemeris' publication or project. It details roles such as Editor, Circulation, Layout, and Proofing, along with the names and contact numbers for each position.

articles.title: Mike Koop
articles.summary: This document outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) telescope loaner program, managed by Mike Koop. It provides detailed lists of telescopes currently on loan, those with extended loan periods, and several immediately available for borrowing by SJAA members. The article also mentions a waiting list for popular scopes and thanks recent donors for adding new equipment to the program.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing options for new or renewal memberships, including standard and junior rates, and an optional add-on for a Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment via check to the treasurer, along with contact information for the organization.
